import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.5

by V. A. Gorbunov

A variety of groups is called *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties is a
variety. Describe all primitive varieties of groups. Is every primitive variety
of groups locally finite?

Here a *variety* of groups is a class of groups defined by a set of identities
(laws) $w(x_1, \dots, x_n) = 1$, and a *quasivariety* of groups is a class of
groups defined by a set of quasi-identities
$u_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_m = 1 \Rightarrow w = 1$, where the $u_i$ and $w$
are words in the free group on countably many variables. (By the theorems of
Birkhoff and Mal'cev these are exactly the classes closed under isomorphic copies,
subgroups, direct products and, respectively, homomorphic images or ultraproducts.)
A variety is *locally finite* if all of its finitely generated members are finite.

Only the yes/no question is formalised. The request to describe all primitive
varieties of groups is not a proposition.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.5»

/-- A class of groups, given as a predicate on groups (with carrier in `Type`). -/
abbrev GroupClass := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law (identity) $w = 1$, where `w` is a word in the free group
on the countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if every substitution of elements of
`G` for the variables (i.e. every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`) sends `w` to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1

/-- A quasi-identity of groups
$u_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_m = 1 \Rightarrow w = 1$: a finite list of premises
$u_1, \dots, u_m$ and a conclusion $w$, all words in the free group on countably many
variables. (Every equation $u = v$ between words is equivalent to $u v^{-1} = 1$, so this
loses no generality.) -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $u_1, \dots, u_m$ of the quasi-identity. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $w$ of the quasi-identity. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies the quasi-identity `q` if for every substitution of elements of `G`
for the variables (i.e. every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`) under which all premises of `q`
become `1`, the conclusion of `q` becomes `1` as well. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, (∀ u ∈ q.premises, φ u = 1) → φ q.conclusion = 1

/-- A class of groups is a *variety* if it consists exactly of the groups satisfying some
set of laws. -/
def IsVariety (𝔙 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔙 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A class of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups satisfying
some set of quasi-identities. -/
def IsQuasivariety (𝔔 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity,
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔔 G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity G q

/-- A variety of groups `𝔙` is *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties (quasivarieties
of groups contained in `𝔙`) is a variety. -/
def IsPrimitiveVariety (𝔙 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsVariety 𝔙 ∧
    ∀ 𝔔 : GroupClass, IsQuasivariety 𝔔 → (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔔 G → 𝔙 G) →
      IsVariety 𝔔

/-- A class of groups is *locally finite* if every finitely generated group in it is finite.
For a variety this is the same as every group in it being locally finite, since varieties are
closed under subgroups. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (𝔙 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔙 G → Group.FG G → Finite G

/-- Every law $w = 1$ is the quasi-identity with no premises and conclusion $w$, so every
variety of groups is a quasivariety. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsVariety.isQuasivariety {𝔙 : GroupClass} (h : IsVariety 𝔙) :
    IsQuasivariety 𝔙 := by
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := h
  refine ⟨(fun w ↦ ⟨[], w⟩) '' S, fun G _ ↦ (hS G).trans ?_⟩
  simp [SatisfiesLaw, SatisfiesQuasiIdentity]

/-- The class of all groups is a variety (defined by the empty set of laws). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isVariety_top : IsVariety (fun _ _ ↦ True) :=
  ⟨∅, fun _ _ ↦ by simp⟩

/-- The class of abelian groups is a variety (defined by the law $[x_0, x_1] = 1$). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isVariety_commGroup :
    IsVariety (fun G _ ↦ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x) := by
  refine ⟨{⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆}, fun G _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesLaw, map_commutatorElement,
    commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  constructor
  · intro h φ
    exact h _ _
  · intro h x y
    have := h (FreeGroup.lift fun n ↦ if n = 0 then x else y)
    simpa using this

/--
Is every primitive variety of groups locally finite?

A variety of groups is called *primitive* if each of its subquasivarieties is a variety.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ 𝔙 : GroupClass, IsPrimitiveVariety 𝔙 → IsLocallyFinite 𝔙 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.5»

  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

  /-- The conclusion word $w$. -/

/-- A group `G` satisfies a quasi-identity if, under every assignment of the variables in `G`
for which all premise words evaluate to $1$, the conclusion word evaluates to $1$. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1) → FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

quotients, and arbitrary direct products. -/
def IsVariety (V : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop :=

  (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), V.Mem G → V.Mem H) ∧
  (∀ (G : Type u) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], V.Mem G → V.Mem (G ⧸ N)) ∧
  (∀ (I : Type u) (G : I → Type u) [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, V.Mem (G i)) → V.Mem (∀ i, G i))

isomorphisms, subgroups, arbitrary direct products, and ultraproducts. In the presence of subgroup

A *variety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws

many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$. By Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes
of groups closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products.
A *quasivariety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of
quasi-identities
$$u_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_n = 1 \implies w = 1 \qquad (n \geq 0).$$
By Mal'cev's theorem these are exactly the classes of groups closed under subgroups,
direct products (including the empty product, the trivial group) and ultraproducts.
A *subquasivariety* of a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a quasivariety contained in
$\mathfrak{V}$. A variety is *locally finite* if every finitely generated group in it
is finite; since a variety is closed under subgroups, this is the same as every group
in it being locally finite.

Only the yes/no question is formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

universe u

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w = 1`, where `w : FreeGroup ℕ` is a word in the
variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables
sends `w` to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises `u = 1`
(for `u ∈ premises`) and a conclusion `conclusion = 1`, all words in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …`. A quasi-identity with no premises is a law. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `u` appearing in the premises `u = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

/-- A group `G` satisfies a quasi-identity `q` if for every substitution `f` of elements
of `G` for the variables under which all premises of `q` evaluate to `1`, the conclusion
of `q` evaluates to `1`. -/
def SatisfiesQuasiIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ u ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f u = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

  ∃ L : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], 𝔙 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ L, SatisfiesLaw G w
